teaser.text: Robinhood Markets, Inc. is a financial-services platform for investing, trading, borrowing and managing money. Its business is easier to understand as a flow: customers bring orders, cash and balances, while counterparties and customers pay for access, financing and services.

stock.title: Robinhood stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Robinhood's stock forecast weighs bear, base and bull scenarios, cash flow after stock pay, and today's earnings and cash valuation.
stock.opening: Robinhood's probability-weighted forecast reaches $89.10 in October 2027 and $93.60 in October 2029. It hinges on trading revenue per unit of activity and net interest spreads.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Robinhood’s business works, who its rivals are, how management allocates capital, and what risks could change the story.

paragraphs.text: The weighted case is $89.10 in October 2027, a -14% return. It is $93.60 in October 2029, a -10% return. The bear case has 30% probability. The base case has 50%; the bull case has 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Robinhood?

paragraphs.text: The bear story is a down-cycle followed by a valuation reset. Quieter trading, weaker monetization, legal limits on event contracts and lower interest spreads reduce profit. The bear price is $43.27 in October 2027 and $32.17 in October 2029. Its probability is 30% because HOOD has three loss-making years in the supplied history and trading revenue remains volume-sensitive.

The bull story requires new products, acquisitions and crypto activity to create durable revenue. Gold, Banking, advisory products and event contracts must deepen customer relationships while legal access holds. The bull price is $135.53 in October 2027 and $187.35 in October 2029. Its probability is 20% because product adoption, integration, monetization and operating leverage must all work together.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Robinhood really make?

paragraphs.text: In 2025, operating cash flow exceeded capital spending, and deducting stock pay produced a lower analytical measure of free cash flow. That measure treats shares issued as compensation as an economic cost to owners, even though no equivalent cash left the company immediately.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Robinhood today?

paragraphs.text: At US$103.99, investors value Robinhood’s common equity at US$93,495.57 million. Its 45.8x trailing P/E means paying US$45.80 for each dollar earned over the past year; its 34.3x forward P/E uses expected earnings for the next year. Those figures imply earnings growth of roughly 34% if the share price does not change. It is like paying US$46 for a shop that earned US$1 while expecting it to earn substantially more soon.

earnings.title: Robinhood earnings: what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Robinhood reports on October 27, 2026; guidance, recent results and ordinary customer activity are the key tests.
earnings.opening: Robinhood’s next results are scheduled for October 27, 2026. Watch whether profit is driven by ordinary customer activity.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers questions about Robinhood’s business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: Robinhood’s weighted price could be $89.10 in October 2027 and $93.60 in October 2029, below today’s price, if operating growth, product economics and legal access hold. Management’s guidance in force covers Adjusted Operating Expenses and SBC for the year to December 2026. It is $2.675–$2.775 billion and was issued July 29, 2026. The range includes Rothera and WonderFi but excludes credit-loss provisions and certain regulatory matters.

blocks.heading: Did Robinhood keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management has also delivered meaningful growth. In February 2025 it expected another year of double-digit revenue growth, and revenue ultimately grew 52%. Its original adjusted expense outlook was US$2.0–2.1 billion; the outcome was US$2.27 billion. The comparison must account for the later addition of acquisition costs and the exclusion of TradePMR from the original plan.

blocks.heading: What have Robinhood’s last eight quarters shown?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose from $989 million in June 2025 to $1,308 million in June 2026. That was 32.3% growth. Operating income rose from $439 million to $574 million, showing that the platform continued to expand.
Net income rose from $386 million to $561 million. Diluted EPS rose from $0.42 to $0.62, but $0.14 of that EPS came from investment gains.

blocks.heading: What should Robinhood watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: The next results release is scheduled for October 27, 2026, after market close, followed by the earnings call at 5 p.m. Eastern. Investors should look for three things together: contributions from the acquired operations, adherence to the expense outlook and profit driven by ordinary customer activity. Strong revenue paired with widening excluded expenses would tell a different story from strong revenue with controlled total costs.
